    You are the construction manager

    Build a data center campus, one phase at a time

    For ages 12 and up · about 20 minutes · no sign-up, no personal data.

    A personal project by Ali Keyvanfar, Ph.D.

    Red Clay Ridge is a made-up site of about 45 acres off a county road in Georgia, next to a street of homes. A company wants a data center campus there. Your job is to build it in the right order, keep the schedule, the budget and the crew safe, and work with the neighbors. The game shows facts and trade-offs. It does not take a side on data centers.

    Pick a phase, place each of its key elements, then finish the phase. Issue cards will interrupt you. Your choices move the dashboard and the neighborhood panel.

    Keys: Tab moves between buttons · Enter or Space presses · N = next step · M = effects on the map on/off · V = voice on/off (these three can be turned off in About) · on the map, arrow keys turn, + or − zoom, and Shift + arrow keys move when zoomed in. While you are siting a piece, drag or tap the map and the arrow keys nudge it, then Set it here. The game asks you to decide when each choice matters.

          Build the Campus

          A personal project by Ali Keyvanfar, Ph.D.

          The site, company and neighbors are made up; the rules and figures in the game are real as of October 2026. Durations are typical ranges and vary by project.

          A companion to Community Builders of Pecan Grove.

          Ages 12 and up (grade 7 to adult); younger players with an adult. Asks no names and stores nothing about you.

          Privacy: this game collects no personal information. No sign-up, ads, analytics or cookies. Nothing you do is sent anywhere. This browser may remember the Library mode, presenter view and shortcut settings, and in class or home mode it keeps your game in progress until the tab is closed. The host logs IP addresses for security, and your browser keeps an offline copy.

          Questions, privacy concerns or corrections: akeyvanf@kennesaw.edu

          Map, keys and modes

          Map: drag to turn; scroll, pinch or press + and − to zoom toward the pointer. Zoomed in, a drag (or Shift + arrow keys) moves the view, and right-drag, Shift-drag or two fingers turn it. The buttons on the map do the same, and Reset view brings the whole site back. To site a piece, drag or tap the map (right-drag or two fingers still turn the view). Green fits the setback, the site and the utility rules. Set it here confirms.

          Modes: with no mode the game is set up for a library kiosk. It starts over after a few minutes without input and saves nothing. Add ?mode=class or ?mode=home to the address to stop it clearing itself and to keep the game in progress if the page reloads, until the tab is closed. ?mode=library starts each game with the voice off.

          How this is scored. Neighbor relations starts at 35 when grading begins. Choices and issue cards add or remove points. The truck traffic, noise and dust & night lighting rows remove points as they rise; after opening, noise always counts at its lowest level, so the cooling type is not scored. The other rows are information only, because they are not the same kind of effect. Safety starts at 82 and moves with your choices and the issue cards. For safety and neighbor relations, 80 or more is Strong, 60 to 79 Good, 45 to 59 Fair, 30 to 44 Watch and under 30 Concern. The schedule is judged against a 45-month plan: Strong at or under 45 months, Good up to two months over, Fair up to four over, Watch beyond that. The budget adds up what your choices and the issue cards cost, plus 0.3% for every month they add to the finish, because crews, equipment and loans keep costing while the work runs late. The plan holds 3% for surprises: Strong at or under 103% of plan, Good up to 104.5%, Fair up to 106%, Watch beyond that. Cooling changes power use and water use on the panel; it is not a point for or against the project.

          Kiosk setup: on a library computer, download the offline kiosk file and open it in a full-screen browser. It is one file with the narration inside, and it works with no network. Opened from the web, this page also saves a copy, and the narration it has played, so a later reload can work offline. Download the offline kiosk file

          Browsers and computers

          Needs a current browser: Chrome or Edge 108 or later, Firefox 101 or later, or Safari 15.4 or later (Mac, iPad and iPhone). The 3D map needs WebGL 2 graphics, which most computers, Chromebooks and tablets in use today have. A screen 1280 × 720 or larger works best; phones show a smaller map. Without 3D graphics the panels, the schedule and every choice still work.

          The game picks less 3D detail on slower graphics. Add ?quality=low to the address if the map is slow, or ?quality=high to always use full detail.

          Words to know

          CM (construction manager)
          the person or firm that plans and runs the building work for the owner. In this game, that is you.
          Critical path
          the chain of steps that sets the finish date. If a step on it slips, the finish slips.
          Long-lead equipment
          equipment built to order, such as large transformers and switchgear, that takes months or years to arrive, so it is ordered during design.
          Substation and transformer
          equipment that steps high-voltage power down for the campus.
          Switchgear
          large electrical equipment that routes and protects the power inside the building.
          MEP (mechanical, electrical & plumbing)
          the systems that power, cool and protect the building.
          UPS (uninterruptible power supply)
          backup batteries that keep the servers running for the seconds before the generators start.
          Silt fence and sediment basin
          a fabric fence and ponds that keep muddy water on the site during earthwork.
          Buffer, setback and berm
          the space between the campus and the homes (the setback is the minimum the county allows), and an earth mound that screens them.
          Tilt-up panels
          concrete walls cast flat on the slab and tilted up into place.
          Dried in
          the roof and walls are closed, so rain stays out.
          Commissioning (Levels 1 to 5)
          testing in steps: factory tests, delivery checks, start-up, functional tests, and an integrated test with a planned power cut.
          Load bank
          a machine that draws power and makes heat the way servers do, for testing.
          Punch list
          the last small fixes before handover.
          Turnover
          handing the finished campus to its owner.
          Megawatt (MW)
          a unit of electric power. 100 megawatts is roughly the electricity of 84,000 homes.
          Contingency
          money held in the budget for surprises.

          For teachers and facilitators: a one-page sheet with learning goals, how to run a session, words to know and debrief questions. Open the educator sheet

          Sources (as of October 2026)

          • Emergency generator testing limited to 100 hours a year: U.S. EPA, 40 CFR 60.4211(f)
          • Georgia Public Service Commission rule for customers over 100 megawatts, adopted 23 January 2025
          • Georgia sales-tax exemption for data center equipment: the 2024 pause was vetoed; in 2026 the repeal bill SB 410 passed the Senate but not the House
          • Background on that exemption: Bloomberg Tax
          • Silt fence and sediment basins before clearing: Georgia construction stormwater permit GAR100001 (summary)
          • Large transformers take about 2 to 4 years to deliver: EE Power, citing Wood Mackenzie
          • Electricity use of large data centers compared with homes: U.S. Energy Information Administration

          Durations are typical ranges, simplified for the game; they vary by project. Real projects overlap their phases; the game runs them one after another, except that utilities run alongside grading and building. The five commissioning levels are common industry practice, not a law or standard.
